subject.title: Feature: Handle Signal message edits (editMessage envelope)

question: Should an inbound Signal edit replace/supersede existing transcript context without creating a new turn, and should edits ever cancel or re-run active work beyond an explicit mention?
rationale: The current inbound pipeline has no established edit-to-transcript or edit-to-active-run policy, so choosing one affects channel consistency and shared session semantics rather than only Signal parsing.

options.title: Define a bounded edit contract
options.body: Specify structured edit metadata, original-message matching, transcript supersession, and default no-reply behavior, with explicit mention handling as the only initial opt-in dispatch path.

options.title: Treat edits as informational only
options.body: Keep normal inbound dispatch but attach an edited marker, accepting duplicate context and potential turn behavior as a documented limitation.

options.title: Fold edits into active-run cancellation
options.body: Design a cross-channel recall/edit lifecycle with the broader work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55691 before adding Signal behavior.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded edit contract
recommendation.body: Specify structured edit metadata, original-message matching, transcript supersession, and default no-reply behavior, with explicit mention handling as the only initial opt-in dispatch path.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal is repeated work on the active Signal inbound monitor and dispatch boundary.
